summary: Apple crostata with breadcrumb streusel: a double batch of crostata dough rolled to fill a half-sheet pan, layered with spiced overlapping apple slices and baked 20 minutes at 400°F, then topped with buttered breadcrumbs and toasted about 5 more minutes; less sweet than pie, serves 12.
glance: 400°F: about 20 minutes, then about 5 more with the breadcrumb streusel
half-sheet (jelly-roll) pan with a double batch of dough
2 cups homemade breadcrumbs, 4 tablespoons melted butter, 2 tablespoons sugar
faq: What is a crostata?

Fussless pie made on a baking sheet instead of in a pie dish, with no need for crimped edges or latticework. A double batch of the author's crostata dough completely fills a half-sheet pan, making it nice for brunch for 12.
Why use breadcrumbs in the topping?

Inspired by an amazing strudel at Forno Marco Roscioli in Rome: breadcrumbs make a variation of streusel. The result is less sweet than a typical pie, a nice match for strong coffee and scrambled eggs.
How do I make the breadcrumbs?

Whiz a few slices of day-old artisan bread such as pain au levain in a blender, tamping down a few times, without reducing them all the way to powder. Don't use canned breadcrumbs, which the author is pretty sure would be terrible.
How do I prepare the apples?

Peel, core and slice into 24 segments each (the author starts with eighths and cuts each into thirds), toss with brown sugar, salt, nutmeg and cinnamon, and arrange in overlapping rows on the chilled, pricked pastry before sprinkling with sugar.
What pan should I use?
The author recommends heavy-duty Chicago Metallic half-sheet pans (jelly-roll pans) that don't warp easily, and silpats if you want non-stick.

summary: Risotto cakes with sherry gastrique: cool leftover risotto bound with one or two beaten eggs, salt and cayenne, shaped into 1/2-inch patties and pan-fried until quite brown, served with crisp sage leaves and a sherry vinegar and sugar reduction; makes 4.
glance: 4 cakes (a light lunch for two, or the basis of a larger meal)
1 or 2 beaten eggs for 1.5 cups of cool leftover risotto
1 cup sherry vinegar and 1/3 cup sugar, reduced until it coats a spoon
faq: How do I make risotto cakes?

Add a beaten egg or two to cool leftover risotto until it holds together, along with salt and cayenne, then shape about 1/3-cup portions into patties 1/2 inch thick and fry on a lightly greased griddle or skillet like pancakes. The author makes extra risotto just for this.
How brown should they be?

They taste better the darker you can get them without burning. Fry until quite brown on the first side, cautiously flip, and cook until finished. You can press panko or sesame seeds into the upper side before flipping.
What is a gastrique?

A reduction of a vinegar or wine with some type of sugar, and often a fruit. This one uses sherry vinegar and white sugar cooked over a moderate flame so the sugar caramelizes, with enough sweetness and acid that a small amount makes an intense counterpoint.
Why make the cakes spicy?
Make them fairly spicy with cayenne to offset the sweetness of the gastrique.
How do I crisp the sage?
Throw the sage leaves in a bit of oil at the edge of the pan and crisp them up.
What else can I serve them with?
Just a bit of good yogurt or creme fraiche.

summary: Cavatelli with slow-roasted broccoli and harissa: broccoli florets and peeled stems pan-roasted slowly in olive oil with garlic and harissa for 45 minutes or more until meltingly tender, tossed with al dente cavatelli and finished with parsley and mint; serves 4, prep 20 minutes, cook 1 hour.
glance: Prep 20 min, cook 1 hr, total 1 hr 20 min
slowly pan-roasted over medium-low heat, 45 minutes or more
1 pound cavatelli, or another small, dense shape
faq: Why cook broccoli for so long?

Many vegetables yield different pleasures depending on time, temperature and technique. Broccoli steamed or boiled for a long time is horrible gray, sulfurous stuff, but slowly pan-roasted in a good amount of olive oil it becomes meltingly tender and luscious, a perfect condiment for al dente pasta.
What is cavatelli and do I need a maker?
A small, fairly dense shaped pasta. The author used a hand-cranked cavatelli maker, but store-bought cavatelli or any other small, dense shaped pasta works.
Why use harissa?
The dish would typically be seasoned with a modest amount of chili flakes, but the author found the more complex flavor of harissa impossible to resist.
How do I finish the dish?

Transfer the al dente pasta to the skillet with the broccoli, reserving a cup of the pasta water, toss over medium-high heat adding some water if dry for moistness and shine, then stir in big handfuls of parsley and mint at the last second.
Do I peel the broccoli stems?
Yes, peel the stems and cut them bite-sized along with the florets.

summary: Zucchini-stuffed zucchini blossoms: caramelized finely diced zucchini mixed with fresh goat cheese, smoked paprika and lime, piped into 16 blossoms, dipped halfway in tempura batter and fried at about 365°F for 30 seconds so the petals still peek out; serves 4 as part of an entree or 8 as an appetizer.
glance: 4 as part of an entree plate or 8 as an appetizer
oil about 3 inches deep at about 365°F, swish about 30 seconds until the batter browns
yield: 4 as part of an entree plate or 8 as an appetizer
faq: How do I keep zucchini blossoms fresh?

The author learned from Alvarez Farms to put them in a plastic produce bag, blow it up like a balloon and tie it tight; this "airbag" protects them from buffeting by the rest of the produce bin and keeps them a day or so.
Where do I find zucchini blossoms?
At farmer's markets, either still attached to tiny zucchini or sold separately. They are expensive by the pound but don't weigh much.
Why stuff them with caramelized zucchini?
The blossoms' flavor is very mild, so the value is in their visual appeal. Caramelizing tiny dice of zucchini amps up the flavor, and goat cheese is a classic pairing.
How do I stuff the blossoms?

Gently untwist and pull apart the petals, pull out the stamens as best you can without destroying the flower, pipe in about 1.5 tablespoons of filling, pull the petals over and give them a little twist.
How do I fry them?

Pick up each by the petal end with tongs, dip about halfway into the tempura batter, let the excess drip, and hold it in the hot oil with the un-battered part out, swishing about 30 seconds until the batter is browned. Drain and season with sea salt.

summary: Sabich, the Iraqi Jewish eggplant sandwich: fried eggplant slices and hard-boiled eggs in pita with hummus, tahina, Israeli salad, pickles, onion, parsley and amba (pickled mango condiment), built to each diner's taste; makes 4 sandwiches.
glance: 1-2 large, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick, fried until tender and browned
4 hard-boiled, 20 minutes in the covered pot off the heat
Israeli salad, hummus, tahina, onion, pickles, parsley, amba
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the egg; gluten-free without the pita, as a salad
faq: What is sabich?

A popular Sabbath food for Iraqi Jews that came with them to Ramat Gan when they emigrated to Israel, and has since gained widespread popularity, with endless variations and arguments about which is best: a pita sandwich of fried eggplant and hard-boiled egg with Israeli salad, hummus, onions, pickles, parsley and amba.
What is amba?

A pickled mango condiment, bright orange. The author found the jarred version a bit harsh and recommends a small amount, or making his quick amba recipe; failing that, use your favorite hot sauce, maybe harissa.
How do I hard boil eggs for sabich?

Put eggs in a pot with cold water to cover, cover the pot, bring to a boil, remove from the heat, sprinkle in a little salt and leave covered about 20 minutes (30 is often cited), then drain, ice bath and peel. The result is soft with no green around the yolk.
How do I build the sandwich?
Fry the eggplant in batches until thoroughly tender and browned, drain on paper towels and salt; put all the other ingredients in bowls so everyone builds their own; toast or grill the pita.
What is the Israeli salad?
A simple salad of finely diced tomatoes and cucumber with lemon juice and salt.

summary: Vegan tempeh-filled potstickers (gyoza): pan-fried tempeh crumbled with browned cabbage, green onion, rice wine, soy sauce and cornstarch, sealed in 48 wrappers, fried 1-2 minutes, steamed about 3 minutes and crisped; yields about 48 in 1 1/2 hours.
glance: about 48 (at least 4 per person as an appetizer)
1 1/2 hours (faster with help forming the dumplings)
1 pound tempeh, cabbage, green onions, rice wine, soy sauce, cornstarch
quick-freeze without touching; cook without defrosting
faq: Why tempeh in vegetarian potstickers?

Where most vegetarian potstickers go wrong is too many vegetables, which add a distracting crunch and leach water. The author's filling is tempeh, sauteed first to develop flavor, then crumbled and mashed with the other ingredients for just the right bite.
How do potstickers get their name?

From the cooking technique: fry the dumplings in a lightly oiled pan until they brown and stick a bit, add water and cover to steam the tops and release the bottoms, then remove the lid and cook off the remaining water.
Why add cornstarch to the filling?
Sprinkled in at the end and tossed through, it absorbs any water released while the dumplings cook.
How do I fold the dumplings?
Moisten the whole edge of a wrapper, put a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center, fold in half and seal, crimping decoratively if you like, and set seal side up on a plate.
Can I make them ahead?
Yes: quick freeze them without touching, bag when solid, and cook later without defrosting, allowing a little more time.
What wrappers should I use?
About 48, one normal package; choose a "thick" variety if possible.

summary: Chickpea and green olive tagine in 20 minutes: onion and chickpeas simmered with chile flakes, ras el hanout, pomegranate molasses and preserved lemon, then marinated pitted green olives, finished with sumac and parsley and served over couscous; vegan, serves 2-3.
glance: 2-3 as a main dish over couscous, or 4 with a roasted vegetable
ras el hanout, pomegranate molasses, preserved lemon, green olives
yield: 2-3 as a main dish over couscous
faq: What is a tagine?
Technically a funnel-shaped clay pot traditionally used in Morocco, but also any moist, spicy stew made with the spices typical of that region.
What is ras el hanout?
A spice mixture of up to 18 spices, used here along with pomegranate molasses, preserved lemon and marinated olives to quickly build big flavors.
What olives should I buy?

Look for a type that is already pitted and marinated in a spice mixture, ideally with Moroccan or Middle Eastern spices, though Sicilian or even French styles will do. Your best bet is the olive bar of an upscale grocer rather than a jar.
How do I serve it?

Family-style over a big platter of steaming couscous for the most dramatic impact, garnished with sumac and parsley. You can add an oven-roasted vegetable such as cauliflower or winter squash to round out a Middle Eastern meal.
How moist should it be?
Moist but not at all soupy: add a few tablespoons of water if needed.

summary: Non-traditional arroz verde: plain medium-grain rice cooked as usual, then stirred with a raw pesto-like puree of parsley, cilantro, oregano, mint or dill, garlic and olive oil, for a vibrant fresh flavor and color; 10 minutes active, 40 total, serves 4.
glance: about 2 cups: parsley, cilantro, oregano, mint or dill
cook rice plain; stir in the raw herb puree and salt just before serving
faq: What is traditional arroz verde?
Rice cooked with a puree of poblano peppers and herbs, which the author finds truly delicious and prefers to the typical red rice found at American Mexican restaurants.
Why not cook the herbs?

The author asked why he was cooking delicious fresh herbs when their raw flavor is so perfect. He omitted the poblanos and made a pesto-like puree of herbs, garlic and a little oil, stirred into the cooked rice, for a vibrant, fresh flavor and matching color.
Can I use the stems?
Yes: because the herbs are thoroughly pureed, tender stems of parsley and cilantro can go in along with the leaves.
Can I change the herbs?
Yes, vary them according to what you have and what you're serving it with. Small amounts of chives and rosemary are also welcome.
How do I add the salt?
1 1/2 teaspoons of Kosher or flaky sea salt (3/4 teaspoon if you use table salt), stirred in with the herb mixture just before serving, then taste and add more.

summary: Grilled eggplant with a raw arrabiata ("angry") salsa of drained cherry tomatoes, garlic, white onion, chile de arbol and olive oil served at room temperature, with eggplant slabs brushed with oil and grilled or roasted at 400°F until thoroughly tender; serves 6 as an appetizer.
glance: 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved, salted and drained 1 hour
2 large or 4 smaller, cut 3/8 inch thick, grilled or roasted at 400°F
salsa at room temperature, within an hour
faq: What is arrabiata?

"Angry" in Italian, referring to the heat from the chilis. The traditional sauce contains onion, garlic, tomatoes and fresh chili peppers: mostly the same ingredients as a fresh Mexican-style salsa, so the author made a raw version.
Why drain the tomatoes?
The author's photo showed the tomatoes releasing liquid, so the recipe has you toss them with salt in a sieve and drain them for an hour. Drink the drained liquid as a cook's treat.
How long can the salsa rest?
Let it rest a while for the flavors to develop. As long as you're serving within an hour, don't refrigerate it: it tastes much better at room temperature.
How do I cook the eggplant?
Brush slices with olive oil and grill, or roast in a 400°F oven, until thoroughly tender; the author says undercooked eggplant is horrible. Choose eggplants that feel heavy for their size.
How should I serve this?
As an appetizer or salad course. If you're grilling, throw the eggplant on first so guests can nosh while you prepare the rest of the meal.

summary: Baked penne with mushrooms and fontina: wilted spinach, penne, two batches of quartered mushrooms browned with garlic, onion, oregano and chili flakes and deglazed with sweet vermouth, stirred with cubed fontina in a 9x13 pan, topped with Parmesan and baked about 15 minutes at 400°F; serves 4 in 45 minutes.
glance: 400°F for about 15 minutes, until bubbly and browned
refrigerate up to 24 hours; 45 minutes to an hour when baked from cold
faq: How is this different from mac and cheese?
It's made with melted cheese instead of a bechamel sauce, so the flavors of the mushroom and spinach come through more clearly.
Why quarter the mushrooms?

Cut in quarters instead of thin slices, they brown nicely on the outside while retaining a satisfying chew. Cook them in two batches in a very hot skillet until well browned but still thick and meaty, not having given up all of their liquid.
Can I change the ingredients?
Use the recipe as a blueprint: any other medium-sized extruded pasta for the penne rigate, any cheese you fancy as long as it melts well, and chard or kale for the spinach.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes, prepare the casserole and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, then bake; from cold it takes 45 minutes to an hour.
How do I wilt the spinach?
Dunk half of it in a large metal strainer in the boiling water about 30 seconds until thoroughly wilted, drain very well and place in the pan; or microwave it.
